1.sense: The surah opens with an oath, and Allah swears by time itself. Whatever else time is, it is the one asset every human being is spending at exactly the same rate and cannot add to.

notes.t: What al-asr means here is not agreed. The age, time in general, the late afternoon and its prayer, and the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ have all been held by serious exegetes. The oath works under every one of them.
notes.src: at-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record the several positions without settling one

notes.t: An oath in the Qur'an is not there to convince a doubter that Allah is telling the truth. It points at the thing sworn by and tells you to look at it, and here the thing is the hour you are currently inside.

links.why: another surah opening on oaths by pieces of time

2.sense: The verdict is given on the whole species and given first, before any exception. Not that man may lose, but that he is in loss, present tense, as a standing condition.

notes.t: Khusr is a merchant's word. It is what you say about a deal that came back with less than went into it. The verse frames a life as a transaction that is currently running at a deficit.
The word is left indefinite, khusrin rather than al-khusr, which in Arabic makes it vast and unspecified rather than a particular known loss.

links.why: the scales, and who is found light

3.sense: Four things pull a life out of deficit, and two of them cannot be done alone. Belief and deeds are between a person and his Lord. Counselling to truth and counselling to patience require somebody else in the room.

notes.t: Tawasaw is a reciprocal form: each counsels the other and is counselled in turn. It rules out a version of this that is only ever given and never received.

Two of the Prophet's ﷺ companions, when they met, would not part until one of them had recited this surah to the other. The report is in at-Tabarani and has been graded authentic by some and questioned by others.
notes.src: at-Tabarani; graded sahih by al-Albani, contested by others

notes.t: Ash-Shafiʿi is quoted saying that if people reflected on this surah alone it would be enough for them. It is a scholar's remark, not a hadith, and it is worth what a scholar's remark is worth.
notes.src: quoted by Ibn Kathir in his commentary on the surah

links.why: the same pairing of faith with mutual counsel to patience and mercy
